stronger_left_out.name: Fly River
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1 met (two counted sources; PNG tourism names it as a great river, Wikivoyage describes river trips from Daru and Kiunga). But a 1,060 km river is a linear feature with no single visitor point: case for: obvious headline feature of the province; case against: Wikivoyage warns passenger boats are not available, no distinct place to stand, pin would be arbitrary (needs a visitor access point, e.g. Kiunga river port).

stronger_left_out.name: Ok Tedi Mine
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: working industrial site, controlled access, Wikivoyage says not to photograph it; nothing a visitor can do.

stronger_left_out.name: Tabubil
stronger_left_out.reason: Fails rule 1 and 2: no visitor source (Wikivoyage, PNG tourism) names it as a stop; re-looked, Wikivoyage mentions it only as the mine corridor with controlled access. A company mine town with no visitor draw.

stronger_left_out.name: Kiwai Island
stronger_left_out.reason: One counted source (Wikivoyage: charter boat trip from Daru to the delta's largest island, 59 km long, villages). For: a real named place, a distinct visit, Wikipedia article with coordinates. Against: single source, needs a charter, a long visit to villages with permission; unclear what a visitor does for half an hour.

stronger_left_out.name: Strickland River
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 3: river as a feature, no visitor point; tourism board mentions it only in the introduction, not as a stop.

stronger_left_out.name: Parama Island
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 1: no visitor source; village island with no stated visitor activity.

stronger_left_out.name: Mount Fubilan
stronger_left_out.reason: Rule 2: the peak no longer exists, replaced by the Ok Tedi pit; no public access.

benchmark: Fly River and Kiwai Island sent to review (long feature / vague trip), as the rules require for journeys beyond a gateway.
